title: Answer: intelligence is shown by active inference, which quantum systems with complex internal flows exhibit generically

statements.text: The framework reads cognition and intelligence off active exploration of the environment, that is, active inference. Every nontrivial agent, a system whose internal dynamics breaks the symmetry of its boundary, is a cognitive system engaged in active inference, and quantum systems with complex enough internal information flows can be expected to behave like organisms. A quantum system with no evident intelligence is then the unusual special case.
statements.scope: Minimal physicalism as a scale-free substrate for cognition and consciousness (2021) and A free energy principle for generic quantum systems (2021)

sources.quote: All nontrivial agents are "cognitive" systems that engage in active inference.
quantum systems with sufficiently complex internal information flows can be expected to exhibit active inference, and hence to behave like organisms.
Indeed, quantum systems that do not display evident intelligence
